items.title: Dawoud Sabu Adeyola interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 30, 2025
items.q: I knew Al but I didn’t know all that about him.

ctx.x: He’s so kind. He’s my second father you know. Yeah you know what? He actually told my father that. He says, ‘cause both of my parents were alive at the time. And sometimes I’d take him by the house you know, because they loved him too. Actually Fanny’s was right around the corner from where my parents used to live you know. And so one time we’re sitting there at the kitchen table having coffee and he tells my dad, he says, “Oh by the way I’ve adopted your son, is that all right? Is that okay with you?” He said,…
That’s great. What a feeling that was to talk to someone who had been in the original production of — you know with George Gershwin of “Porgy & Bess.” Like that just really blew my mind.

Yeah I mean that’s cool, but to me his association with Charlie Parker man. You know? That Bird actually mentioned him in a couple of books, like Ross Russell’s Bird Lives. When Bird actually says that the reason that he — when he visited New York with Jay McShann back in the early ‘40s, and he decided to stay in New York because he went to a jam session at Monroe’s and he heard a new form of music being played under the leadership of a pianist named Allen Tinney. And that made him want to stay in New York and…
